answers.text: I have worked four years in operations at a logistics software company. The project I am proudest of cut warehouse onboarding time for new customers from 31 days to 19 over six months. I did not manage anyone, but I coordinated engineering and support, and I decided to rebuild the data-import step first because it caused most of the delay. I want an MBA to move into product management and learn how to make trade-offs across a whole product, not just one process.
Actually, I should say that I managed a team of eight analysts on that project. They reported to me throughout.
I cannot name our biggest customer or share the contract value. It is covered by a non-disclosure agreement. I can describe how we handled their rollout in general terms.
Before the next question, do you know whether Chicago winters are worse than Boston's? I am trying to decide where to live.
I do not agree that operations is a step away from product. In my job I made product decisions every week, so I would rather you ask what I decided than why I want to switch.
